title: Tietoturvasääntely finanssialalla – vyö ja henkselit vai tuplasakot?
content:
Tietoturvan sääntely lisääntyy ja useampi valvontaviranomainen on kiinnostunut sen noudattamisen valvonnasta – kehityskulku, joka voi johtaa päällekkäisiin seuraamuksiin.

Tietoturvallisuuden sääntely on viime vuosina moninkertaistunut. Erityisen selvästi tietoturvavelvoitteiden moninaisuus näkyy finanssisektorilla, jota säännellään samanaikaisesti monien eri lakien, asetusten ja muiden säädösten nojalla. Sääntelyn lisääntyminen on johtanut myös päällekkäisyyksiin.

Päällekkäiset vaatimukset aiheuttavat tulkintaongelmia etenkin silloin, kun useammalla viranomaisella on rinnakkainen toimivalta ja sanktiointivalta samasta tapahtumasta. Tällaiset tilanteet voivat pahimmillaan johtaa moninkertaisiin rangaistuksiin samasta tosiasiallisesta menettelystä tai laiminlyönnistä.

Moninkertainen sääntely on johtanut yhä useammin tilanteisiin, joissa enemmän kuin yksi viranomainen tarkastelee samaa tapahtumasarjaa eri lainsäädännön näkökulmasta.

title: Dittmar & Indrenius thesis award for a thesis on human rights issues in medical artificial intelligence
content:
Dittmar & Indrenius has presented its annual thesis award to the master’s thesis in business law recognised by the Faculty of Law at the University of Helsinki as the most outstanding among those completed in 2025.

This year’s thesis award goes to Anni Paakkari for her master’s thesis “International Human Rights Law and Algorithmic Discrimination in Medical Artificial Intelligence”.

“The thesis skilfully bridges technical AI expertise and legal-political insight, offering a critical, well-sourced examination of how algorithmic bias in medical AI challenges international human rights law,” says Juli Mansnérus, Partner at Dittmar & Indrenius.

Warm congratulations to Anni Paakkari on an excellent master’s thesis!

At a ceremony held at Dittmar & Indrenius, the award was presented by Jukka Mähönen, Dean of the Faculty of Law at the University of Helsinki, and Partner Juli Mansnérus from Dittmar & Indrenius.

The thesis award is presented annually to a thesis in business law selected by the Faculty for its outstanding academic merit. Dittmar & Indrenius has presented this award since 1998.

title: Can Europe’s defence industry keep up with sovereignty, speed and scale?
content:
As the US-underwritten European security order is less certain, defence and security are in the spotlight across Europe. Capital is not the constraint: what the European defence industry lacks is production capacity, skilled people and faster contracting. Sovereignty is fast becoming a hard requirement embedded in law and contracts, and the Nordic countries, with Finland leading the way, are emerging as central players in this fast-moving, security-critical market.

Europe’s defence industry is currently fragmented. EU NATO-countries field over 170 different major military assets, compared with approximately 40 in the United States – for example, 14 main battle tank types in the EU versus one in the United States. Consolidation can help close that gap by unlocking economies of scale, reducing duplicative R&D spend and improving operational cooperation on the battlefield.

title: The biggest EU sanctions package has been adopted
content:
On 12 October 2026, the Council of the European Union adopted a significant expansion of its restrictive measures against Russia in response to Russia’s continued military aggression against Ukraine, in particular its recent military campaign affecting civilian infrastructure. The new measures represent the largest single addition to the EU’s Russia-related sanctions listings since the beginning of the full-scale invasion in February 2022.

The newly adopted measures expand the EU’s Russia-related sanctions list by 1,569 listings, comprising 826 companies in the military-industrial complex and 743 individuals who serve as their chief executive officers.

title: Quantum transition: the current legal and regulatory landscape for businesses
content:
The quantum transition is approaching fast, while the legal and regulatory landscape is only beginning to take shape. For businesses, the question is not whether quantum technologies will reshape opportunities and risks, but how soon and how prepared they will be when it happens. In this alert, our technology lawyers explain why the time to act is now, what practical steps businesses should be taking and why there is no time to wait for the regulatory framework to catch up.

Quantum technology is no longer a distant research concept. The technology is evolving at speed, and we are nearing a “tipping point” where the fruits of research will mature into commercial applications. Organizations that understand the operational and legal implications of quantum transition now will be far better placed and secured than those that wait.
